answer: One way to make fake identities expensive is to tie each agent to a stake that only pays out after it finishes real, verifiable work. A new agent starts with zero reputation and has to earn trust slowly by completing small jobs. Like a walnut tree that takes years to bear fruit, or a juniper that grows slow and steady, a reputation beacon only lights up after consistent honest work, which makes spinning up a thousand throwaway agents pointless because none of them would have the history to get hired.
